title: AI Media Studio V2 · Model Guide
note: Catalog ids match GET /models. Drop this JSON next to the frontend or fetch it from /model-guide.json. Taglines are routing hints, not Fal marketing.

sections.label: Text → Image
sections.blurb: Generate a still from a prompt. Nail start/end frames here before you spend on video.

models.label: Flux 2 Pro
strengths: Studio-grade photoreal. Default T2I in V2.
weaknesses: Type and infographics lose to Qwen / Recraft.

models.label: Flux 2 (cheaper)
weaknesses: Softer than Pro on hard details.

models.label: Flux 2 Flex
strengths: More control / quality tradeoff than base Flux 2.
Useful when Pro is too locked-in.
weaknesses: Still a photoreal family, not illustration.

models.label: Flux 1.1 Pro Ultra
strengths: Good when Flux 2 Pro feels small.

models.label: Seedream 5.0 Pro
strengths: Pairs with Seedream 5 Pro edit / sheets.
weaknesses: Photoreal faces can later trip Seedance R2V.

models.label: Seedream 5.0 Lite
strengths: Same family as Pro for promote-up.

models.label: Seedream 4.5
models.tagline: Best for detailed listing stills (prior gen)
weaknesses: Superseded by 5 Pro for most new work.

models.label: Nano Banana 2
strengths: Fast Google T2I with resolution control.

models.label: Nano Banana Pro
strengths: Good when the prompt must stick.

models.label: Qwen Image 3
models.tagline: Best for type, signage, and faces
weaknesses: Not the photoreal listing king (use Flux / Seedream).

models.label: Recraft V4
strengths: The design tool in a photoreal catalog.
weaknesses: Don't send Recraft frames into Seedance as 'real' people.

models.label: Grok Imagine 2.0
models.tagline: Best for xAI stills in the same stack

models.label: Fibo Gen 1.5
models.tagline: Best licensed T2I for type and control
weaknesses: No inspire-from-ref in this wiring (v1 is prompt T2I).

sections.label: Image → Image
sections.blurb: Edit a source still. Staging, wardrobe, sky, cleanup.

models.label: Fibo Edit 1.5
strengths: 1–4 images: Image 1 is the source; 2–4 are refs.
weaknesses: Furniture pop-in is a test case — Flux 2 Pro / Nano Banana Pro stay primary for locked architecture.

models.label: Fibo Edit (v1)
models.tagline: Single-image local edit with optional mask
strengths: Targeted changes (furniture, sky, cleanup) without a full rewrite.
weaknesses: Single image only — use Fibo Edit 1.5 for refs.
No region box — mask still or prompt only.

models.label: Flux 2 Max (edit)
strengths: When Pro's first pass isn't enough.
weaknesses: Est. ~$0.07 first MP — spendy vs Pro.

models.label: Flux Kontext Pro
strengths: Local + scene transforms from one still.
weaknesses: Strict aspect_ratio enum — mismatches get snapped.
Single image, not a ref pack.

models.label: Nano Banana Pro (edit)
weaknesses: Can rewrite more than you asked vs Kontext.

models.label: Nano Banana 2 (edit)
weaknesses: Weaker lock than Pro on hard prompts.

models.label: Seedream 5 Pro (region)
strengths: Up to 10 refs on the family.
weaknesses: Heavier than a Flux Pro dab.
Whole-frame restyles may prefer Flux / Banana.

models.label: Qwen Image 3 (edit)
models.tagline: Best for editing type and faces

models.label: Grok Imagine 2.0 Edit
weaknesses: Older Grok edit SKUs still sit in the catalog — prefer this one.

models.label: Grok Imagine Quality Edit
models.tagline: Best Grok edit for detail and text
strengths: Stronger detail and text than the cheap Grok edit.
weaknesses: Superseded in spirit by 2.0 — keep if Quality wins a shot.

models.label: MAI-Image-2.5-Pro (edit)
weaknesses: Less V2 battle-testing than Flux / Banana.

sections.label: Reference → Image
sections.blurb: Edit with extra reference stills (identity, style, product).

models.label: Flux 2 Max (edit)
strengths: When Pro's first pass isn't enough.
weaknesses: Est. ~$0.07 first MP — spendy vs Pro.

models.label: Nano Banana Pro (edit)
weaknesses: Can rewrite more than you asked vs Kontext.

models.label: Nano Banana 2 (edit)
weaknesses: Weaker lock than Pro on hard prompts.

models.label: Qwen Image 3 (edit)
models.tagline: Best for editing type and faces

models.label: Grok Imagine 2.0 Edit
weaknesses: Older Grok edit SKUs still sit in the catalog — prefer this one.

models.label: Grok Imagine Quality Edit
models.tagline: Best Grok edit for detail and text
strengths: Stronger detail and text than the cheap Grok edit.
weaknesses: Superseded in spirit by 2.0 — keep if Quality wins a shot.

sections.label: Region edit
sections.blurb: Grounded, boxed, or layer edits instead of a whole-frame rewrite.

models.label: Seedream 5 Pro (region)
strengths: Up to 10 refs on the family.
weaknesses: Heavier than a Flux Pro dab.
Whole-frame restyles may prefer Flux / Banana.

sections.label: Text → Video
sections.blurb: Prompt to a clip. Native audio on most flagship models.

models.label: FLUX 3
strengths: Draft then enhance to cut cost.
BFL on fal — V2 already wired.
weaknesses: Extend is a separate SKU and costs more than the I2V rate.

models.label: Seedance 2.5
models.tagline: Best for long single-shot T2V (up to 30s)
weaknesses: Photoreal people can trip the face filter on related R2V.

models.label: Wan 3.0
weaknesses: No Prime SKU in this wiring.

models.label: Veo 3.1
strengths: Highest quality T2V in the catalog.

models.label: Veo 3.1 Fast
strengths: Good default when you might still want Veo.
weaknesses: Not as pretty as full Veo.

models.label: Kling 3.0 Pro
strengths: Storyboard maps Shots to native multi_prompt (customize or intelligent cuts).
weaknesses: V2 currently prices Standard T2V the same as Pro — treat Pro as the real SKU until that's fixed.

models.label: Kling 3.0 Standard
strengths: Storyboard multi_prompt like Pro (no @Element tray — T2V schema has no elements).
weaknesses: Estimate currently matches Pro ($2.52 / 15s). Prefer O3 Standard if you want a real cheaper Kling.
Don't trust the Standard discount until the helper is fixed.
use_cases: Only if you confirm a real price gap

models.label: Kling O3 Pro
weaknesses: O3 vs 3.0 naming is easy to mix up in the dropdown.

models.label: Kling O3 Standard
weaknesses: Less polish than O3 Pro / 3.0 Pro.

models.label: Grok Imagine 1.5
weaknesses: Not the listing default (H3 / FLUX 3 / Kling).

models.label: Luma Ray 2
weaknesses: Duration/aspect follow Luma, not the Fal flagship set.
use_cases: When you want a Luma look

models.label: Mirage Avatar X (script)
weaknesses: Needs a face/identity path for lock (use R2V).

sections.label: Image → Video
sections.blurb: Animate a start still. Best path for a character you already trust.

models.label: FLUX 3 I2V
strengths: Animates a still, aspect follows the plate.
weaknesses: Identity lock is weaker than H3 Omni / Seedance R2V.

models.label: Seedance 2.5 I2V
strengths: Prefer I2V start-frame over R2V for photoreal people.
weaknesses: R2V face filter is a different SKU — this I2V path is the safer Seedance route for characters.

models.label: Wan 3.0 I2V
strengths: Start still required; optional last frame.
weaknesses: Not an identity pack (use R2V for multi-ref).
use_cases: First→last without a dedicated bridge SKU

models.label: MiniMax H3 I2V
weaknesses: JPEG proxy before upload can soften fine detail.
use_cases: First→last without a dedicated bridge SKU

models.label: Kling 3.0 Pro I2V
strengths: Elements tray: frontal + extra stills or a motion clip, cited as @Element1.
Storyboard maps Shots to multi_prompt (customize / intelligent cuts).

models.label: Kling 3.0 Standard I2V
strengths: Same 3–15s family, actually cheaper than Pro on I2V ($1.68 vs $2.10 / 15s).
Same Elements (@ElementN) + Storyboard multi_prompt as Pro.

models.label: Kling O3 Standard I2V
strengths: Cheapest Kling I2V in the set.

models.label: Kling 2.6 Pro I2V
models.tagline: Best older Kling with native audio
weaknesses: Superseded by 3.0 / O3 for new work.

models.label: Veo 3.1 I2V
strengths: Cinematic I2V. Keep architecture in the prompt.

models.label: Grok Imagine 1.5 I2V
strengths: Strong motion + native audio from a start still.

models.label: LTX 2.5 Pro I2V
strengths: Native audio. Optional last frame on Fast sibling.

models.label: FLUX 3 First→Last
strengths: Bridges two stills with native audio.

sections.label: Reference → Video
sections.blurb: Lock subject/style from a pack of stills (and sometimes video/audio).

models.label: MiniMax H3 Omni
strengths: Storyboard default — photoreal people stay usable.
weaknesses: Don't recycle last-frame as next-shot ref (false face hits on other models).

models.label: Wan 3.0 R2V
strengths: Cite Image 1 / Image 2 (character vs scene) in the prompt.

models.label: Seedance 2.5 R2V
models.tagline: Best multimodal ref pack — avoid tight photoreal faces
strengths: Up to 50 refs (image/video/audio), up to 30s, native audio.
weaknesses: Photoreal Seedream faces often flag as real people. No safety-off on fal 2.5.
Prefer I2V start-frame or H3 Omni for characters.
use_cases: Long R2V when the plate isn't a headshot

models.label: Grok Imagine 1.5 R2V
weaknesses: Weaker omni than H3 (no video/audio refs).

models.label: Veo 3.1 Reference
weaknesses: ~$0.40/s, 8s (catalog enum is 8s only on this row).

models.label: Mirage Avatar X R2V
strengths: Needs a voice/audio ref (optional talking-head still).
weaknesses: No duration enum — quotes will scale to whatever you send.

sections.label: First → Last
sections.blurb: Bridge two stills into one move. Connect shots, room-to-room.

models.label: FLUX 3 First→Last
strengths: Bridges two stills with native audio.

sections.label: Video → Video
sections.blurb: Edit or retake an existing clip. Length usually follows the source.

models.label: Kling O3 Standard V2V
weaknesses: Helper will quote 60s if you send it — clamp to source length.

models.label: LTX 2.3 Retake
strengths: Regenerate a 2–16s segment, lock surrounding motion.

models.label: FLUX 3 Extend
strengths: Continue a clip with prompt + audio.
weaknesses: Estimate currently uses the I2V rate ($2.55 / 15s) — real extend is costlier.
use_cases: Add a beat after a hero

models.label: sync-3 Lipsync
weaknesses: Not a generator. Needs a decent face take.
use_cases: Match VO to a talking head

sections.label: Extend
sections.blurb: Continue a clip. Prompt plus native audio on FLUX 3.

models.label: FLUX 3 Extend
strengths: Continue a clip with prompt + audio.
weaknesses: Estimate currently uses the I2V rate ($2.55 / 15s) — real extend is costlier.
use_cases: Add a beat after a hero

models.label: MiniMax Music 2.6
weaknesses: 15s and 60s estimates currently match ($0.15) — likely capped.

models.label: Google Lyria 3 Pro
strengths: Up to 3 min, commercial use on fal.
Flat per track (duration doesn't change the quote).
weaknesses: No per-second control in the estimate.
use_cases: When you want a Google song, not a timed bed

sections.label: Sound effects
sections.blurb: Whooshes, rooms, hits. Keep it short.

sections.label: Voiceover
sections.blurb: TTS for listing reads and avatar scripts.

models.label: MiniMax Speech 02 HD
weaknesses: Empty prompt still shows a stub cost.

models.label: ElevenLabs Eleven v3
models.tagline: Best natural TTS with acting tags
weaknesses: Stock voices only in this row.

models.label: Topaz Upscale (image)
weaknesses: ToolNode shows a static catalog cost — it does not re-quote on factor.

models.label: Topaz Wonder 3.5
weaknesses: Can invent detail — don't use on legal photos.

models.label: FLUX Video Upscale
weaknesses: Confirm precise vs creative tier at run time.

models.label: Topaz video (Proteus / Artemis / Nyx / Starlight / Gaia)
models.tagline: Best Topaz video finish — quotes are placeholders
strengths: Real Topaz SKUs are in the dropdown (denoise, restore, CG, generative).
weaknesses: V2 currently shows $0.10 / 5s / 1080p for almost every Topaz video SKU. Don't trust the number.
ToolNode does not re-estimate on duration.
use_cases: Pick the named SKU for the job; treat cost as TBD

sections.label: Finish / restore
sections.blurb: Denoise, restore, deblur, interpolate, lipsync, talking heads.

models.label: sync-3 Lipsync
weaknesses: Not a generator. Needs a decent face take.
use_cases: Match VO to a talking head
